correctness.rationale: The product distance formula is exact. The low-scale core B is a full-fiber simplicial blow-up of VR(Cn;r-1), with dominated-vertex collapses, and the finite-cycle circle theorem applies since n>=3r>3(r-1). A pair of columns at circular distance exactly r forces equal-row endpoints; their common adjacent columns are precisely the intervening interval except the unique exceptional third column when n=3r. This partitions every noncore face into a unique full interval simplex or one of mr maximal triangles. Each interval simplex admits an explicit elementary free-face collapse relative B using its nonempty interior. Every exceptional attaching loop represents the generator of pi1(B)=Z, because its three edges are homotopic to one complete clockwise row-cycle. Attaching mr disks of degree +-1 yields wedge^(mr-1) S2. The extracted standard-library verifier independently enumerated full clique complexes and computed exact F2 homology for 16 finite instances; no finite computation substitutes for the parameter-uniform proof.

value.rationale: The 2025 toroidal-grid Rips literature isolates resonance phenomena for equal-side finite toroidal grids; the graph K_m square C_n gives a natural anisotropic, complete-fiber family, including the previously untreated thin torus C3 square Cn. Determining whether such spaces retain one loop or grow higher-dimensional sphere homology is a motivated topological gap. The classification is sharp at circumference n=3r for every r>=2, with an exact unbounded multiplicity mr-1 from a geometric attaching-map mechanism, not an isolated table value or substitution of an existing formula. It makes a genuinely new homotopy claim beyond finite rank tests.
